title: Volver a ser Elda: the Banana Belt, the Command of Frente 47, and the Road Back to a Name
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Nueva Antioquia, Turbo: one of twelve
stops.date_confidence: attested in both the Spanish and English Wikipedia articles; her own 2025 memoir gives 15 October 1967 and a different corregimiento, and the two records are left standing against each other
stops.campa: In the corregimiento of Nueva Antioquia, in the municipality of Turbo, a girl is born into a campesino household of twelve children. Uraba is the whole horizon: the gulf, the plantations that feed Europe, the union halls, the disputed land. They name her Elda Neyis Mosquera Garcia. Sixty two years later she will publish a book whose title asks for that name back. In between there are twenty four years in which the war calls her something else, and the country learns the other name first.
stops.quote_source: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: The corregimiento of Nueva Antioquia, Turbo, in the Uraba banana belt

stops.name: Currulao, Turbo: the other birth record
stops.date_confidence: given in her 2025 memoir and irreconcilable with the 15 August 1963 birth at Nueva Antioquia carried by both Wikipedia editions; recorded as an open contradiction, not adjudicated
stops.campa: Her memoir opens with a date and a place the encyclopedias do not carry. She sets her birth at Currulao, a corregimiento of the same municipality, on 15 October 1967, four years and two months after the record the reference works give. Nothing in the reachable sources reconciles the two. The Currulao corridor runs north from Apartado through the banana farms, and it will hold her again in the nineties, when she comes back through it as a fighter in the country she was born in.
stops.quote: Nací en Turbo, Antioquia, en el corregimiento de Currulao, el 15 de octubre de 1967
stops.quote_source: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: Currulao, corregimiento of Turbo, named as her birthplace in the memoir
sources: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, 'Volver a ser Elda' (Debate, 2025), publisher preview

stops.name: Apartadó: the Juventud Comunista
stops.date_confidence: she states the ages twelve and sixteen to El Colombiano and gives no year; 1975 is calculated from the 1963 birth date and would move to 1979 under the memoir's 1967. Apartado anchors the regional pattern and is not a documented meeting place
stops.campa: At twelve she meets the Communist Youth and stays in it until she is sixteen. Apartado in those years is the capital of the Uraba labor question, its unions and its funerals, and the recruiters of the guerrilla work the same streets as the organizers. She says later that the ideology moved her less than the distance did: what she wanted was to be far from the house. The doctrine arrives afterward, in the camps, taught to a girl who has already decided to go.
stops.quote: A mí no me motivaba tanto la ideología comunista, me motivaba más estar lejos de casa.
stops.quote_source: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: The Juventud Comunista Colombiana cells of the Uraba banana municipalities in the 1970s
sources: El Colombiano, launch interview with alias Karina (4 October 2025)

stops.name: Turbo: the food left on the stove
stops.date_confidence: the departure scene is undated in the memoir excerpt; placed at the 1984 entry into the FARC-EP that Spanish Wikipedia and El Colombiano both give, with the day defaulted
stops.campa: She cooks one morning for the boy in the house, sets the food on the stove, and goes. There is no farewell scene in her telling and no ceremony. There is breakfast, and then the mountains. The household she leaves is poor and she knows it is poor, and the guerrilla feeds and clothes whoever walks up to it. Behind her the banana zone goes on producing for Europe. Ahead of her is a column of Frente 5, which will teach her to march, to carry, to shoot, and to answer to a name she has not chosen.
stops.quote: Una mañana le cociné al muchacho, le dejé la comida en el fogón y me fui para la guerrilla.
stops.quote_source: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: The family house at Turbo, left on the morning of her enlistment
sources: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, 'Volver a ser Elda' (Debate, 2025), publisher preview

stops.name: Turbo: the father's one condition
stops.date_confidence: undated in the sources; placed at the departure, which itself is fixed only by the disputed 1984 enlistment year
stops.campa: Her father does not want her to go. He argues, and he loses, and when he sees she is going anyway he reduces everything he has left to say to a single sentence: the only thing I ask of you is that you be a good guerrillera. She will command a front, lose an eye, carry a price on her head, and sit before a tribunal, and the sentence survives all of it intact. It is the only instruction anyone in the family gives her about the war, and it asks her to be good at the thing he could not stop her doing.
stops.quote: Lo único que yo le pido es que sea una buena guerrillera.
stops.quote_source: Her father, quoted in Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: The father's parting words, the memoir's opening moral instrument
sources: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, 'Volver a ser Elda' (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
La FM, interview with alias Karina

stops.name: Chigorodó: into Frente 5
stops.date_confidence: the year 1984 and the unit Frente 5 are attested in Spanish Wikipedia; Chigorodo is a reconstruction standing for a Frente 5 town, since no source names her enlistment site, and the parallel claim that she joined at sixteen sits unreconciled beside the year
stops.campa: She enters the FARC-EP and is put into Frente 5, the column that holds the banana municipalities of Uraba. The organization she joins was formalized in 1964 out of the peasant self defense groups of La Violencia, the convulsion Fidel Castro walked into in Bogota on 9 April 1948 and Che Guevara crossed in 1952, calling the capital a city under a leaden peace. She arrives twenty years after the founding, when the front is an institution with quartermasters, courts, and a rank a girl from Turbo can climb.
suggested_refs: Frente 5 of the FARC-EP, the guerrilla column of the Uraba banana municipalities
sources: El Colombiano, launch interview with alias Karina (4 October 2025)

stops.name: The Currulao corridor: the naming
stops.date_confidence: the memoir excerpt neither dates nor locates the naming; placed early in her first year, with the corridor pin standing for the Frente 5 camps of the Turbo banana zone
stops.campa: A guerrillera called Erika stands three new women in a line and hands out their war names in one breath: you will be called Viviana, you Deisy, and you Karina. The third name is the one Colombia will learn. Seventeen years before this morning, in Bolivia, Tamara Bunke had died under a war name handed to her by the same practice, and is remembered as Tania. Elda Neyis Mosquera is now Karina, and stays Karina for twenty four years, until a book takes the first name back out of the war.
stops.quote: usted se va a llamar Viviana, usted Deisy y usted Karina
stops.quote_source: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: The FARC practice of assigning noms de guerre on entry, recorded in the memoir
sources: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, 'Volver a ser Elda' (Debate, 2025), publisher preview

stops.name: Chigorodó: five loads of firewood
stops.date_confidence: undated and unlocated in the memoir excerpt; placed in her first months and pinned to the same representative Frente 5 town as the enlistment
stops.campa: She does not put on the armband when the order comes, and the sanction is five trips for firewood. She carries them. She sets down afterward what she thought while carrying them: at home she gathered wood because she wanted to, and if she did not want to she did not gather it, and here everything is by obligation. The house she left was poor, and nobody in it gave her orders. The column feeds her and takes every decision that is left over. She stays.
stops.quote: en mi casa cargaba leña porque quería, si no quería no buscaba leña. Aquí todo es por obligación
stops.quote_source: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: The disciplinary regime of a FARC column, as recorded from inside it
sources: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, 'Volver a ser Elda' (Debate, 2025), publisher preview

stops.name: The Currulao corridor: the assembly
stops.date_confidence: the scene is undated and unlocated in the memoir excerpt and is corroborated by nothing outside it; the year and the pin are placements within her early Frente 5 service
stops.campa: The commanders put a question to the assembled guerrilleros. A man named Gonzalo has killed a woman named Maribel, and the column is asked what should be done with him. She records the answer in the first person plural and does not soften it: we all answered, kill him. This is the internal law of the front, voted by the people it governs and executed by them. She is one of the voices in the vote, and she writes it down forty years later without exempting herself from it.
stops.quote_source: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: The consejo de guerra of a FARC column, as narrated by a participant
sources: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, 'Volver a ser Elda' (Debate, 2025), publisher preview

stops.name: Currulao: the daughter
stops.date_confidence: El Colombiano's launch interview gives the year 1991 and no month; the birthplace is not named in any reachable source and the pin follows her Frente 5 corridor
stops.campa: A daughter is born to her in 1991 and grows up somewhere else. The war does not accommodate a child and she does not leave the war. When the girl is five, paramilitaries take her, and the child gets away from them and lives. Karina learns this at a distance, as she learns everything about her daughter, through couriers and rumor and the intervals between operations. The two of them are given back to each other much later, after the surrender and after the sentences.
suggested_refs: The daughter born in 1991, kidnapped at five by paramilitaries and escaped
sources: El Colombiano, launch interview with alias Karina (4 October 2025)

stops.name: La Chinita, Apartadó: the massacre
stops.date_confidence: attested; her personal role is named by Spanish Wikipedia's article on the massacre among the commanders held to account, and the coordinates sit inside Apartado rather than on the barrio itself
stops.campa: On the night of 23 January 1994 men of Frente 5 enter the barrio of La Chinita, in Apartado, and open fire on a neighborhood party. Between thirty five and thirty seven people are killed, most of them workers and former militants of the Esperanza, Paz y Libertad demobilization. Elda Neyis Mosquera is named among the former commanders held to account for it, alongside Joverman Sanchez Arroyave, Ruben, who led the front. It is the act that follows her name longest in Uraba.
suggested_refs: The La Chinita massacre of 23 January 1994, barrio Obrero, Apartado

stops.name: Churidó, Apartadó: the running war
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested and the month is not; coordinates are the corregimiento centre of Churido rather than any named site of combat
stops.campa: Combat is recorded at Churido in 1995. The corregimiento sits in the plantation flat between Apartado and Carepa, and the front fights there against the army and against the paramilitary blocks coming up the axis from the south. Uraba in these years holds four armed structures, one trunk road, and a banana crop that has to be cut and shipped on schedule through all of it. She is a combatant of the middle rank, learning the command she will be handed three years from now.
suggested_refs: Churido, corregimiento of Apartado, in the contested plantation flat

stops.name: Carepa: the town twice
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested and the month is not; the day and month default and the pin is the municipal seat
stops.campa: Fighting reaches Carepa in 1995. It is an ordinary banana town on the trunk road, and it is also the seat of the Seventeenth Brigade of the National Army, the formation her front exists to fight. She passes through it as a combatant. Years after the surrender she will be kept inside that same brigade's headquarters, under the protection of the army she attacked here, while the courts decide what she is. The second visit puts her inside the gate she once counted as a target, and the town itself is unaltered.
suggested_refs: Carepa, Antioquia, banana town and seat of the Brigada XVII

stops.name: Finca Osaka, Urabá: an entry on the list
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested and nothing else is; the farm is not geocoded in any reachable source and the coordinates are an acknowledged Uraba-zone placeholder
stops.campa: An operation at the farm called Osaka enters the record for 1996, one line among the combats credited to her by the encyclopedias and the charge sheets. The farm itself has left almost nothing behind: no fixed location, no account of what happened there, no count of the dead. It survives as a name on a list. Much of her war exists in exactly this form, a place and a year and a verb, assembled afterward by prosecutors out of testimony given by the people who were standing on the other side of it.
suggested_refs: The finca Osaka operation of 1996, a place-name surviving only on a charge sheet

segments.name: Frente 47: the Eye and the Command

stops.name: Pavarandó Grande, Mutatá: the right eye
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested and the month is not; the coordinates are Pavarando Grande itself, correcting an earlier placement that named Mutata's seat and matched neither
stops.campa: A grenade goes off near her in combat at Pavarando Grande in 1998 and takes her right eye. She does not leave the front. The photographs on the wanted notices and in the newspapers all work from the missing eye, and the country learns her by it: the one eyed commander is a figure in the press long before she is a defendant in a courtroom. She is thirty five, or thirty one, depending on which birth record is true, and she has ten years of war ahead of her and fourteen behind.
suggested_refs: Pavarando Grande, corregimiento of Mutata, site of the 1998 grenade wound

stops.name: The Caldas corridor: command of Frente 47
stops.date_confidence: the year, the unit and the bloc are attested; no source names a place or a month, and the pin is a reconstruction anchored on Sonson in the eastern Antioquia and Caldas corridor where Frente 47 actually operated
stops.campa: In 1998 she is given Frente 47 of the Bloque Noroccidental, a front that works Antioquia, Caldas, and Risaralda, and she becomes one of the very few women in the FARC to hold a command of that weight. The war moves with her out of the banana flat and up into the cold corridor: Sonson, Aguadas, Marulanda, Pensilvania, coffee country and paramo. For the next eight years the attacks that make her name are planned here, and the army's maps carry a woman's alias where a man's would ordinarily sit.
suggested_refs: Frente 47 of the Bloque Noroccidental, operating across Antioquia, Caldas and Risaralda
sources: Infobae, coverage of 'Volver a ser Elda'

stops.name: Juradó, Chocó: the fusiliers' post
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested, day not given and defaulted; the pin is the municipal seat of Jurado and not the position itself
stops.campa: In December 1999 her front overruns a fusiliers battalion position at Jurado, on the Pacific coast at the Panamanian border. Twenty five soldiers are killed and twelve are taken. It is the largest single action attributed to her, executed at the far western edge of the country, hundreds of kilometers from the corridor where the front normally works. The Choco coast is jungle and river and no roads, and a column that can strike there and vanish is a column the army cannot fix in place.
suggested_refs: The Batallon de Fusileros position at Jurado, taken in December 1999

stops.name: Arboleda, Pensilvania: thirteen police
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested, day not given and defaulted; Arboleda is a corregimiento of Pensilvania in Caldas and the pin anchors on the municipal seat, no source geocoding the corregimiento itself
stops.campa: In July 2000 she directs the taking of the corregimiento of Arboleda. Thirteen police officers are killed. Of everything charged against her this is the operation the courts fasten on first: nine years later a judge converts it into thirty three years of prison, on charges of aggravated homicide, terrorism, rebellion, aggravated theft, and damage to property. Arboleda is a street of houses in the coffee mountains of Caldas, and it holds a police post because the state has to hold something there.
suggested_refs: Arboleda, corregimiento of Pensilvania, Caldas, taken in July 2000

stops.name: Cerro Montezuma, Pueblo Rico: the base on the ridge
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested, day not given and defaulted; the coordinates are Cerro Montezuma itself rather than Pueblo Rico's town centre
stops.campa: In September 2000 Frente 47 overruns the army base on Cerro Montezuma, on the ridge above Pueblo Rico in Risaralda, some eleven kilometers northwest of the town and high over the Pacific slope. Thirteen soldiers are killed and twenty are wounded. A base like this one exists to watch the corridor between the Choco jungle and the coffee departments, which is the corridor her front lives in, and taking it is a military act and an argument about who the mountain belongs to.
suggested_refs: The Cerro Montezuma army base above Pueblo Rico, Risaralda

stops.name: Rural Caldas: the June incursion
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested, day not given and defaulted; the sources name no municipality and the coordinates are an acknowledged central Caldas placeholder, a genuine gap
stops.campa: In June 2002 an incursion into Caldas leaves thirteen police officers dead. The sources that carry the count do not carry the municipality. It falls in the worst year of the war: the talks at the Caguan collapse in February, Alvaro Uribe is elected in May on the promise of finishing the FARC by force, and the fronts answer by taking towns. Hers is one of the fronts taking towns, in a department of steep coffee roads where a police post is the only state for a day's walk in any direction.
suggested_refs: The June 2002 Caldas incursion, municipality unnamed in the sources

stops.name: Caldas: eight killed, thirty taken
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested, day not given and defaulted; no place at all is named for this operation and the pin repeats the central Caldas placeholder, which is a reconstruction
stops.campa: In December 2005 she takes part in a joint operation in which eight police officers are killed and thirty more are captured. Thirty prisoners turn a raid into an administrative problem: the column has to feed, guard, move, and eventually trade a small crowd of men. By this year the army's Plan Patriota is pushing the fronts off the roads and up into the high country, desertion is running steadily, and the arithmetic of the war has turned against her while the operations themselves still succeed.
suggested_refs: The December 2005 joint operation, location unrecorded in the sources

stops.name: Montebonito, Marulanda: five dead
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and corroborated by El Espectador; the coordinates are Montebonito itself, correcting an earlier pin that matched neither the corregimiento nor Marulanda's seat
stops.campa: On 4 March 2006 Frente 47 takes the corregimiento of Montebonito, in Marulanda, the cold high municipality that gave the founder of the FARC his nom de guerre. Five people are killed, among them an infant of seven months, ten are wounded, and ten houses burn after a short circuit during the fighting. It is one of the last large actions before her surrender. Two years remain, and they are the two years in which the front she commands comes apart from the inside.
suggested_refs: Montebonito, sole corregimiento of Marulanda, Caldas, taken 4 March 2006
sources: El Espectador, coverage of the Montebonito attack (March 2006)

stops.name: The Caldas corridor: the arithmetic
stops.date_confidence: the killing of Ivan Rios in March 2008 is attested; the bounty figures are not, and the pin is the reconstructed Frente 47 corridor rather than a documented location for any of this
stops.campa: By 2008 she is worth more dead than alive to the people standing next to her. The press carries a figure of nine hundred thousand dollars on her head, attached to no government and traceable to no document. After she deserts, the FARC is reported to put three hundred million pesos on her in turn. In March her fellow commander Ivan Rios is killed by his own chief of security, who cuts the hand from the body and carries it to the army for the reward. She reads the arithmetic correctly.
suggested_refs: The killing of Ivan Rios by his own security chief, March 2008
sources: Infobae, coverage of 'Volver a ser Elda'

stops.name: Medellín: the surrender
stops.date_confidence: the date, the two companions and the rifle wound are attested; the receiving body is contested, Spanish Wikipedia naming the DAS and English Wikipedia the military, and neither names the city, so the Medellin pin is inferred from the press conference and is a reconstruction
stops.campa: On 18 May 2008 she walks up to a security office with two other guerrilleros, one of them her partner and the chief of her security, and gives herself up. She carries a rifle wound in her right arm. The commander of Frente 47 ends twenty four years in the organization by walking toward the state instead of away from it. The front has been shedding fighters for months. The woman the army has hunted longest arrives on foot, of her own accord, and asks for the paperwork.
suggested_refs: The surrender of 18 May 2008, receiving agency contested between the two encyclopedias

stops.name: Medellín: the press conference
stops.date_confidence: English Wikipedia places the news conference in Medellin around the May 2008 surrender and gives no day; 19 May is a placement immediately after the attested surrender, not an attestation, and the underlying report is the Los Angeles Times of 20 May 2008
stops.campa: She sits in front of the cameras in Medellin and gives her reasons: the pressure of the army, the deterioration of the guerrilla, and the fear that her own troops would kill her for the money on her head, as Ivan Rios was killed by his bodyguards weeks before. It is the sentence the state most wants said aloud, and she says it herself, unprompted, in the city from which the Uraba war was administered at both ends. From this room forward she is a public person rather than a hunted one.
suggested_refs: Los Angeles Times, FARC commander surrenders in Colombia, 20 May 2008
sources: Los Angeles Times, 'FARC commander surrenders in Colombia' (20 May 2008), cited via English Wikipedia

stops.name: Bogotá: thirty three years for Arboleda
stops.date_confidence: month and year attested, day not given and defaulted; no source names the city for this ruling and the canonical Bogota pin of the corpus stands in for the judicial district. This is an ordinary criminal conviction, not the Justicia y Paz process
stops.campa: In February 2009 a court sentences her to thirty three years for Arboleda: aggravated homicide, terrorism, rebellion, aggravated theft, damage to property. She pleads guilty and takes the reduction. The capital has been sentencing women for taking up arms against the government since Policarpa Salavarrieta was shot in its main square in 1817, and it drove Manuela Saenz out of the country that outlived her general. The charge sheets have changed. The venue has not.
suggested_refs: The February 2009 ordinary criminal conviction for the Arboleda attack

stops.name: Bogotá: gestora de paz
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in English Wikipedia; the venue of the announcement is not named and the canonical Bogota pin stands in for it
stops.campa: On 6 March 2009, four weeks after the sentence, she is released under conditional liberty on one condition: that she work as a promoter of peace, a gestora de paz, and persuade the fighters still in the mountains to come down. The state has understood what it holds. A commander who deserted is worth more talking than jailed, and her voice, saying to the columns what she said to the cameras in Medellin, is the instrument. She accepts the condition and begins the work.
suggested_refs: The conditional release of 6 March 2009 and the gestora de paz condition

stops.name: Buga: forty years
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested in Spanish Wikipedia, the month and day are not and are defaulted; the pin is Buga's town centre standing in for the specialized circuit court
stops.campa: In 2010 a specialized court in Buga, in the Valle del Cauca, hands her forty more years for further actions of Frente 47. She is at that moment working publicly for demobilization under a government commission. Neither fact cancels the other: the Colombian state is at once employing her as an argument and convicting her as a defendant, and it goes on doing both for another twelve years. Buga is far from the corridor where the acts were done, and hears the case because the circuit sits there.
suggested_refs: The specialized circuit court of Buga, Valle del Cauca, and its 2010 forty year sentence

stops.name: Brigada XVII, Urabá: held until 2017
stops.date_confidence: Spanish Wikipedia gives only an end year, 2017, with no start date and no municipality beyond Uraba; the Carepa pin is a reconstruction resting on the brigade's known seat, and the detention is not reconciled with her 2009 conditional release
stops.campa: She is held at the headquarters of the Seventeenth Brigade of the National Army in Uraba until 2017: the same brigade her front fought, in the same region she was born in, and, for a woman the FARC has condemned as a traitor, the safest address in the country. The banana flat is thirty kilometers wide and she has now occupied every position available in it, campesina, combatant, commander of a front, prisoner of the state, and finally guest of the army that hunted her.
suggested_refs: The Brigada XVII headquarters at Carepa, seat of her custody until 2017

stops.name: Bogotá: the Sala de Justicia y Paz
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested and the June dating follows the Semana report of 10 June 2022 cited through Spanish Wikipedia, which could not be reached directly; the number of co-defendants is given as eight by RCN Radio and ten by El Colombiano
stops.campa: In 2022 the Justice and Peace chamber of the Bogota high court convicts her together with a group of other former combatants, and she becomes the first FARC commander sentenced under that framework. She asks the victims for forgiveness. The proceedings sit inside the apparatus the 2016 accord built, the same machinery of searches and reparations that in that same year sent the state out looking for the bones of Camilo Torres Restrepo, the priest who left the university for the ELN and was killed in 1966.
suggested_refs: The Sala de Justicia y Paz of the Tribunal Superior de Bogota and its 2022 ruling
sources: Semana, 10 June 2022, cited via Spanish Wikipedia (page unreachable: connection refused)

stops.name: Medellín: the sewing machine
stops.date_confidence: the dressmaking work is attested without a date or a city and the pin is a reconstruction; the 2016 completion of eight years of alternative sentencing and the request for continued protection are separately reported by Infobae
stops.campa: After the release she works as a dressmaker. The commander of Frente 47 measures shoulders and sets sleeves in a city she used to enter only under a war name. She gives interviews, speaks about demobilization and reincorporation, and becomes a recognizable voice for the people who came down from the mountains after her. The threats do not stop. In 2016 she completes eight years of alternative sentencing and asks the state to leave her protection detail in place.
suggested_refs: Semana profile, Karina, la desmovilizada de las Farc que mas persiguieron las autoridades
sources: Semana profile of Karina, as summarized in secondary coverage
Infobae, coverage of 'Volver a ser Elda'

stops.name: Bogotá: the forums
stops.date_confidence: no single appearance is documented at this point; the decade is general in the coverage and the pin and the year are both reconstructions standing for a pattern of appearances through the 2010s
stops.campa: Through the 2010s she appears at forums and on national television, arguing for the peace process and for the reintegration of former fighters. The country listens to her in a particular way: not as a repentant civilian but as somebody who ran a front, who knows what a column decides at four in the morning, and whose face carries the evidence. She is asked the same question in every studio, and the answer she gives is the one the state licensed her to give in March 2009.
suggested_refs: Her public appearances as a voice for reincorporation through the 2010s
sources: General Colombian media coverage of Karina after 2009, summarized in secondary sources

stops.name: Medellín: Volver a ser Elda
stops.date_confidence: the launch interview in El Colombiano carries a timestamp of 4 October 2025, which fixes the release to that month and corrects an earlier September dating; the pin follows the newspaper's city and not a documented launch venue
stops.campa: In October 2025 she publishes Volver a ser Elda, written with the researcher Gustavo Duncan out of some sixty hours of recorded conversation and roughly two years of editing, under the Debate imprint. The title is the whole argument: to go back to being Elda, which requires that Karina be set down. She says the FARC never forgave her desertion and has never stopped seeing her as a traitor. It is the first version of her life told in her own order.
stops.quote: Las FARC nunca perdonaron mi deserción y no han dejado de verme como una traidora.
stops.quote_source: Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, Volver a ser Elda (Debate, 2025), publisher preview
suggested_refs: Volver a ser Elda: una biografia intima de alias Karina, Debate, October 2025
sources: El Colombiano, launch interview with alias Karina (4 October 2025)
Elda Neyis Mosquera García with Gustavo Duncan, 'Volver a ser Elda' (Debate, 2025), publisher preview

stops.name: Medellín: twenty four years
stops.date_confidence: the figure of twenty four years and the regret are confirmed in the El Colombiano launch interview; the verbatim wording circulated elsewhere could not be located in a reachable page and the sentiment is attributed rather than quoted
stops.campa: In the interviews around the launch she puts a number on it: twenty four years in the FARC, and she regrets them. The organization, she says, did harm to the society it claimed to be fighting for. She is sixty two, or fifty eight. She has been a combatant longer than she has been anything else, and she is now doing the slow civil work of being a person who used to be Karina, in a country that has not settled what to do with the people it fought and then licensed to speak.
